title: test(driver-sql): pin the varchar-sizing type switch against spec's BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES
body:
Fixes #12017

`packages/spec` decides which field types may **declare** a `maxLength`
(`BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`, read by `FieldSchema` and by objectql's
record-validator since #11989 / #11875). `driver-sql`'s `varcharColumnChars` /
`createColumn` switch decides which types get a column **sized from** that
declaration. The two are related by reasoning and nothing asserted the
relationship. This PR adds the missing edge. **No runtime code changes.**

⛔ **No divergence exists today** — the two lists were re-measured on this base
and they agree. This is a missing guard, not a live defect, and a green run
proves nothing on its own. The load-bearing evidence is the ablation section.

## The relationship the guard asserts, in the form it asserts it

Over the spec's whole `FieldType` vocabulary:

```
{ t in FieldType.options : varcharColumnChars sizes t from the field's own maxLength }
    ===  BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES
```

Set **equality**, and both directions are load-bearing:

- **⊇** is the card's failure mode. A member of spec's set the switch does not
  size is a declared bound the column ignores — it falls to the catch-all
  `table.string(name)`, knex's varchar(255). The author declares
  `maxLength: 2000`, the platform formally accepts it, the column refuses at
  255. That is the #11431 defect re-entering through a different door.
- **⊆** is its mirror image, and the reason this is not a subset check. A type
  the switch sizes from `maxLength` while `FieldSchema` **refuses**
  `maxLength` on it is sizing code no authored metadata can reach — and, in
  the TEXT branch, an unbounded column whose bound no write seam enforces,
  which is the exact invariant #11794 admits text-family members under.

Measured on this base: both sides are the same twelve types — `text`,
`textarea`, `email`, `url`, `phone`, `password`, `markdown`, `html`,
`richtext`, `code`, `signature`, `qrcode`.

### ⭐ The asymmetry the assertion is scoped around

The naive form — *"spec's set equals the union of the driver's two branches"* —
is **false as stated**, and a guard written that way would go red on day one
for a reason that is not the defect.

`'string'` is in the switch's varchar branch and in **no** spec set, because it
is not a spec type at all: `FieldType.options` opens at `'text'` and has no
`'string'` member (verified against a positive control — `FieldSchema` = 14
hits in the same file). It is what `field?.type || 'string'` supplies when a
field declares no type — knex's **builder** name. So the equality is scoped to
the declared vocabulary, and a second assertion pins `'string'` as that untyped
default (a field with no `type` at all must get the same answer as one typed
`'string'`), so the scoping is a stated fact rather than a convenient omission.

## Route: pin, not derive — argued on measurement

The card and triage left this fork open. Both candidate premises turned out to
need correcting, and I checked rather than inherited them:

- **`driver-sql` may import from `@objectstack/spec`.** It already does, at
  runtime, as a production `dependencies` entry — `sql-driver.ts` imports
  `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`, `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`, `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` and
  `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES` and composes them into `JSON_COLUMN_TYPES`, whose own
  comment reads *"Membership is owned by @objectstack/spec — a type added there
  becomes a JSON column here without touching this file."* So derivation is not
  merely permitted here, it is this file's existing idiom. That removes the
  doubt; it does not settle the fork.
- **`@objectstack/lint` is the wrong home** — confirmed by reading its contract,
  not inherited as a guess. Its README states the dependency direction is
  one-way `lint -> @objectstack/spec` and that it *"never depends on a
  runtime"*. `driver-sql` is a runtime.

**I chose the pin, and the reason is that the two questions are different.**
#12119's two derivations (the write-seam validator and the refusal message)
both answer the *same* question spec's constant answers — "which types does the
write seam bound?". The driver asks a different one — "which physical column
shape?" — and `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` does not carry the varchar/TEXT
partition that second question needs. A derivation would therefore have to
**invent** a default for every future member (TEXT), at the one seam where the
choice has consequences the maintainer has actually ruled on per type: #11794
measured the text family's membership, #11875 ruled `signature`/`qrcode` in by
name. A pin goes red at the moment that decision is needed instead of supplying
an unchosen answer silently — and, unlike a derivation, it also holds the ⊆
direction.

On the four axes: the **business need** is measured, not speculative — #12119
had to hand-edit this switch to admit two types, and nothing would have caught
it if that edit had been forgotten. **Long-term soundness** favours the pin: it
keeps column-shape business logic out of `packages/spec` (Prime Directive 2)
and makes the coupling explicit and checkable rather than implicit. For
**AI-authored metadata**, a loud red at the authoring point beats a consumer
that quietly defaults — a deriving consumer inventing the half of the answer
the producer does not carry is the tolerant-consumer shape this repo refuses.
**Scope discipline**: one test file, no runtime dependency, no new surface.

## No fourth hand-maintained list

The branch a type takes is **read off the driver's own dispatch**, never
restated here — a copied case list is the very defect this card is about, and
is what the #11794 pin had to accept (its `UNBOUNDED_UNKEYED` spells out 36
type names). Three probes at a declared bound of 700 separate four outcomes:

| branch | unkeyed | keyed |
|---|---|---|
| `declaredVarcharLength` (varchar from the declaration) | 700 | 700 |
| `keyableTextLength` (TEXT unless keyed) | `null` | 700 |
| catch-all — declaration **ignored** | 255 | 255 |
| not sized from metadata (JSON / virtual / primitives) | `null` | `null` |

The keyed probe is what makes the text family distinguishable from "not sized"
at all — unkeyed, both answer `null`, and that conflation is exactly why the
#11794 pin needed a hand list. 700 is not arbitrary: it is wider than
`DEFAULT_STRING_VARCHAR_CHARS` (255) so an ignored declaration is visible, and
inside both `MAX_KEYABLE_VARCHAR_CHARS` (768) and `MAX_VARCHAR_CHARS` (16383)
so neither ceiling mis-classifies a type. An answer outside the table throws
rather than falling into a bucket.

## What the two existing pins do NOT cover

- `sql-driver-11565-row-byte-budget.test.ts` pins the width **mirror** against
  `createColumn`. Both sides are the driver, so a type that fell to the
  catch-all satisfies it perfectly: the mirror says varchar(255) and the column
  **is** varchar(255).
- `sql-driver-11794-richtext-text-family.test.ts` pins the driver's
  unbounded-when-unkeyed set against a hand-written list **in that file** — the
  driver pinned against itself, one copy further out.

Neither reads the spec's set. The ablations below demonstrate this rather than
assert it.

## ⭐ Ablations — the load-bearing evidence

Direction and exact count were **predicted in writing before each mutation**.
Every mutation was confirmed on disk by counting both the removed text and the
injected text; every restore is proven byte-identical to the `HEAD` blob
(`git hash-object` compared against `git rev-parse HEAD:path`), and each script
carries a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restore with absolute paths. The subject
resolves through relative source specifiers and this package's vitest config
aliases `@objectstack/spec/*` to spec's **source**, so no `dist/` sits between
the mutation and the runner.

**A — driver-side removal.** `case 'qrcode'` renamed out of *both* switches.
Predicted RED, 2 of 3. **Observed: exactly that** — the set equality failed
naming `- "qrcode"`, the physical test failed with
`+ "qrcode: declared 700, landed varchar(255)"`. Control: **#11565 stayed
GREEN**, both its sides having moved together. (#11794 went red here, since
`qrcode` is in its hand list — which is why A is not the decisive one.)

**B — driver-side addition, the ⊆ direction.** `case 'secret'` added to the
varchar branch — a type spec deliberately carves out (ADR-0100). Predicted RED,
1 of 3. **Observed: exactly that** — set equality failed naming `+ "secret"`.
Controls: **#11565 and #11794 both GREEN**. Caught by this guard alone.

**C — the card's own failure mode, and the decisive one.** The spec admits a
new type and the driver is never taught about it. Created **in memory**
(`BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES.add('color')` from a temporary setup file) so that
**zero bytes of the read-only `packages/spec` were touched** — verified by
`git status --porcelain -- packages/spec` empty before and after. The setup
logged `setSize=13 hasColor=true`, so the drift really existed in-process.
Predicted RED, 2 of 3. **Observed: exactly that** — `- "color"` from the set
equality and `+ "color: declared 700, landed varchar(255)"` from the physical
test. Controls: **#11565 and #11794 both GREEN** — a spec-side addition is
invisible to both existing pins, and visible only to this one.

A first attempt at C via `vitest --setupFiles` died with
`CACError: Unknown option --setupFiles` (no such CLI flag in vitest 4). That
exit 1 is recorded as **NOT MEASURED**, never as a result — it never reached
the guard. It was re-run through a temporary config extending the package's own.

## Verification

Gate union derived from the **actual** changed paths with
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (the
script reads its own change set from the merge base), run at `c7ff8127`, which
is the head of this branch. 22 path-matched families plus the
convention-triggered test-file kind. Every exit code was captured **before any
pipe**; verdicts quoted are the gates' own printed lines.

All green, including: `check:cross-package-test-inputs`
(*"OK: 20 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared"*),
`check:test-source-alias`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:where-matcher`
(*"307 matcher(s) discovered ... none new"*), `check:query-options-erasure`,
`check:objectql-double-limit`, `check:published-files`,
`check:type-source-resolution`, `check:driver-conformance`
(*"OK — 50 covered cell(s), 0 in the DEBT ledger"*), `check:nul-bytes`
(*"scanned 7057 text file(s) ... no raw ASCII control bytes"*),
`check:page-declaration-shape`, `check:slot-lookup`,
`check:comment-mask-adoption`, `check:plugin-teardown-shape`,
`check-ci-filter-parity`, and the changeset family
(`check-empty-changeset` — *"1 declaring changeset(s) added"* —
`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`,
`check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:objectui-changeset`,
`check:pm-half-states`).

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec tsc --noEmit` exits 0 **and really
covers the new file**: the package's tsconfig has no test exclusion, and
`--listFiles` shows the new test among the 555 files in the program — measured
rather than assumed, since a typecheck that excluded it would be a true
statement about nothing.

`sql-driver-12017-...`, `sql-driver-11565-...` and `sql-driver-11794-...`:
**3 files, 12 passed, 3 skipped** (the skips are the opt-in live MySQL/Postgres
cells) on the restored tree at `c7ff8127`.

### Declared narrowings

- **The full `@objectstack/driver-sql` suite was not run**, only the new file
  and the two neighbouring pins it composes with. No source file changed in
  this PR, so no existing test's subject moved; CI runs the suite in full
  regardless.
- `check:type-check-debt` (convention-triggered) was **not run**: its ratchet
  half needs the whole workspace closure built and refuses outright otherwise.
  That refusal would be **NOT MEASURED**, not green, so it is named here rather
  than counted. The structural question it guards is answered above — the new
  test file sits inside an existing tsc program.

## Composition

This guard pins mirror ↔ spec. #11565 pins mirror ↔ `createColumn`. Together
they give `createColumn` ↔ spec, which is why the switch-level assertion is
sufficient — and the third test asserts the invariant against a real column
anyway, with an in-run control (`color`, declaring 700, landing varchar(255))
so that a green cannot mean "this table never showed a 255 to begin with".
